title: Grex (grog squad)
heading: Grex
summary: Defines the grex as the small unit of grogs that accompanies magi on expeditions, and how greges relate to the turb as permanent or newly assembled squads.
quotes: A grex typically numbers up to six individuals

title: Custos (favored grog)
heading: Custos
summary: Explains the custos, a favored grog set apart by skill, great deeds or loyalty and given better provisions and pay, and that custodes count as specialists when building a covenant and working out its finances.
quotes: Custodes are usually equated to specialists when building a covenant

title: Servants
heading: Servants
summary: Describes the indoor and outdoor servants who keep a covenant running and how the Covenants book ties the number of servants and teamsters to the covenant's population, with laborers and craftsmen reducing outgoings.
quotes: two servants and one teamster are needed to support two magi, three companions, or ten soldiers

title: Personal Servants
heading: Personal Servants
summary: How a magus's personal servant differs from a specialist, how the role gives status among the covenfolk, and a table of suitable servant types for different kinds of magus.
quotes: Performing all these services for a magus is the mark of the personal servant
related: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.113

title: The Chamberlain
heading: The Chamberlain
summary: The chamberlain coordinates the servants, is treated as a specialist, uses the Profession: Chamberlain Ability, and can raise or lower the covenfolk's Prevailing Loyalty by mediating the effects of The Gift.
quotes: Governing the servants of a covenant is covered by the Profession: Chamberlain Ability
boosts the Prevailing Loyalty of the covenfolk

title: The Covenant Rolls
heading: The Covenant Rolls
summary: Records of past covenant accounts that serve as a summa for Profession: Chamberlain and a growing encyclopedia of Area Lore: Covenant, can be researched with a roll, act as an Arcane Connection to the covenant if removed, and may be incomplete or damaged.
quotes: The rolls serve as a summa for the Profession: Chamberlain Ability, typically with a Quality of 6.
make an Intelligence + Area Lore: Covenant roll with an Ease Factor related to the obscurity of the information sought

title: Specialists
heading: Specialists
summary: Specialists are the covenfolk with focused skills beyond daily upkeep or defense, bought with covenant build points; the entry also explains when a craftsman counts as a servant rather than a specialist.
quotes: specialists are bought with covenant build points (**ArM5**, page 72)

title: Agents
heading: Agents
summary: Agents are specialists placed away from the covenant as sources of information or remote help; they are bought with build points but their wages are folded into the general budget unless there are unusually many.
quotes: they need not be included in the covenfolk roster when it comes to determining finances

title: The Steward
heading: The Steward
summary: The steward sees to the needs of the specialists, uses Profession: Steward (often with Leadership), and like the chamberlain can soften or aggravate the covenfolk's reaction to The Gift.
quotes: The role of steward is governed by the Profession: Steward Ability

title: The Autocrat
heading: The Autocrat
summary: Describes the autocrat, a single officer who combines the roles of chamberlain and steward and commands all non-military covenfolk.
quotes: he is in command of all the non-military covenfolk

title: Soldiers
heading: Soldiers
summary: Soldiers defend the covenant; they need roughly equal Combat Totals to fight as a trained group, and companions are rarely counted among them. Also notes the Code of Hermes limits on lending soldiers to feudal lords.
quotes: soldiers need to train together and have roughly equal Combat Totals to fight effectively as a trained group

title: The Turb Captain
heading: The Turb Captain
summary: The turb captain leads all of the covenant's soldiers, is provisioned as a specialist at least, and may be treated as a companion character even when designed as a grog.
quotes: A turb captain is provisioned as a specialist at least

title: Unit Sergeants
heading: Unit Sergeants
summary: Sergeants command smaller units of the turb, are chosen for loyalty and the Leadership Ability, and are treated as specialists for wages, food and lodging.
quotes: Sergeants are rewarded by being treated as specialists with respect to wages, food, and accommodation.

title: The Drill Sergeant
heading: The Drill Sergeant
summary: The drill sergeant trains the grogs to fight as a trained group by teaching a Martial Ability each year, keeps order and administers punishments, and needs Leadership and Teaching.
quotes: This involves providing a season of teaching in a Martial Ability (usually Single Weapon) over the course of each year.

title: Accelerated Group Training
heading: Accelerated Group Training
summary: A leader rolls to shorten the time a group needs to practice together before it counts as a trained group, against an Ease Factor set by how much training time is available; failure delays the group until season's end and a botch wastes the season.
quotes: Stress die + Communication + Leadership
When the training period is complete, they can function as a trained group (see **ArM5**, page 173).

title: Other Military Ranks
heading: Other Military Ranks
summary: Describes the intermediate corporal-like rank between soldier and sergeant, represented by the Custos Social Status Virtue, and how temporary expedition roles can become semi-permanent.
quotes: This rank is represented by the Custos Social Status Virtue.

title: A Noble Household
heading: A Noble Household
summary: Lays out the household offices (steward, chamberlain, marshal and their subordinates) a large covenant can copy to organize its servants and specialists.
quotes: the three chief officials in a noble household are the steward, the chamberlain, and the marshal

title: Military Hierarchy
heading: Military Hierarchy
summary: Organizes covenfolk into squads of soldiers and auxiliaries, with the Roman manus, decuria and centuria given as an example chain of command.
quotes: the covenfolk are divided into squads, each of which consists of soldiers and their auxiliary staff

title: Nations (organizing covenfolk)
heading: Nations
summary: Lets a covenant divide its grogs into nations that cut across servant, specialist and soldier roles, formed by family, ethnic group or location, with members often holding a Loyalty Personality Trait specific to their nation.
quotes: The identifying feature of a nation is that it cuts across roles.

title: Guilds (organizing covenfolk)
heading: Guilds
summary: Describes organizing grogs by function into guilds, with larger covenants using more defined guilds, and points to the Guild Covenant Hook if the troupe wants guilds that can withdraw their services.
quotes: the Guild Covenant Hook (*Covenants*, page 19) can be bought if this situation is desirable

title: Professional Guilds
heading: Professional Guilds
summary: Models covenant guilds on craft, service and merchant guilds, grouping those with the same or allied Craft or Profession Abilities and laying out the guild ranks from dean down to apprentices.
quotes: A guild consists of all craftsmen that use the same or a group of closely allied Craft or Profession Abilities.

title: Monastery (organizing covenfolk)
heading: Monastery
summary: A guild-like structure where department officials can requisition manpower and funds as needed instead of having their own permanent staff, suited to small covenants.
quotes: This is a good model for a small covenant

title: Watch Patterns
heading: Watch Patterns
summary: Charts for single and double duty showing which watch and patrol is on duty, off duty or free at each time of day, so the storyguide can randomly determine which grogs are on watch when an event occurs.
quotes: randomly determine what patrol (night or day) and watch (first to fourth) a character is in

title: Duties (watch, off duty and free time)
heading: Duties
summary: A soldier's time is split into duty, off-duty and free time, with the turb divided into day and night patrols who periodically swap, and with sub-patrols assigned to areas such as wall, gate and keep.
quotes: A soldier's time is divided into three periods: duty (or watch duty), off-duty, and free time.

title: The Watches
heading: The Watches
summary: Gives the named eight watches of the day and night with their start times, and explains how patrols rotate through normal sentry duty and double duty.
quotes: The 24 hours of the day are divided into eight watches of three hours each: four day watches and four night watches.

title: Sentry Duty (staying awake on watch)
heading: Sentry Duty
summary: Rules for grogs on watch: what they may and may not do, how Fatigue is handled, the Stamina + Concentration roll to stay awake, the Awareness penalty for sleeping sentries, and the penalty after being woken suddenly.
quotes: This involves a Stamina + Concentration roll; failure indicates that the character is dozing or asleep.
Stamina + Concentration + simple die
Characters who are asleep have a –9 penalty to any Awareness rolls.

title: Double Duty
heading: Double Duty
summary: When trouble is expected, longer shifts are ordered and each grog makes a dusk Fatigue roll whose Ease Factor rises with each double-duty watch; failure costs a Long-Term Fatigue level, and none are regained until normal shifts or long uninterrupted sleep.
quotes: Stamina + simple die versus Ease Factor 3 + number of double duties

title: Off Duty
heading: Off Duty
summary: What grogs do when off duty: drill with the drill sergeant, maintain kit, take work crews or errands, and can fit in Practice with an Ability; also covers the meals and daily ration provided.
quotes: If he gets time to himself with all this going on, a grog can put in some Practice with a particular Ability.

title: Free Time
heading: Free Time
summary: Free time is when grogs sleep; a grog who does not sleep during it loses a Long-Term Fatigue level until he sleeps long enough, and drinking the ration is only allowed just after coming off duty.
quotes: a grog who does not sleep in his free time suffers a Long-Term Fatigue level until he manages to sleep for at least two continuous watches

title: Rewards
heading: Rewards
summary: Explains how covenants reward skill, good behavior and bravery, usually through the turb captain, steward or chamberlain, who choose and announce the reward.
quotes: it is good for morale if the covenant is seen to reward skill, good behavior, initiative, and uncommon bravery

title: Improved Rations
heading: Improved Rations
summary: Better food as a reward, which if kept for a full year improves the grog's Living Conditions Modifier on aging rolls.
quotes: A grog spending a year on improved rations receives a –1 improvement to his Living Conditions Modifier when making aging rolls.

title: Improved Equipment (reward)
heading: Improved Equipment
summary: Superior arms, armor or tools given as a reward, which may be of Expensive cost or give actual bonuses, and are lost if the grog is demoted.
quotes: This equipment might be Expensive rather than Standard cost

title: Promotion In Rank
heading: Promotion In Rank
summary: The highest reward: a grog can rise to custos, then sergeant or equivalent, and perhaps captain, chamberlain or steward, gaining better food, lodging, pay and pension.
quotes: A standard grog can be promoted to custos

title: Punishments
heading: Punishments
summary: How covenants discipline covenfolk in public, how corporal and privilege-withholding punishments differ, and how fair, proportionate punishment avoids losing Prevailing Loyalty while frequent or unjust punishment makes covenfolk hostile to the magi.
quotes: does not usually result in a loss of Prevailing Loyalty

title: Reduction of Rations (punishment)
heading: Reduction of Rations
summary: Reduced food as a punishment; seasons spent on reduced rations in a year worsen the grog's Living Conditions Modifier for aging.
quotes: A character who spends one or more season a year on reduced rations suffers a +1 penalty to his Living Conditions Modifier

title: Flogging
heading: Flogging
summary: A public punishment with a strap that inflicts Light Wounds and Long-Term Fatigue losses depending on the number of blows.
quotes: 1, 2, or 3 Light Wounds are inflicted by this punishment

title: Whipping
heading: Whipping
summary: A harsher punishment of lashes with a long or short whip that inflicts Light, Medium or Heavy Wounds by number of lashes, with a limited recovery time before pay is docked.
quotes: 10 lashes inflicts a Light Wound, 30 lashes a Medium Wound, and 50 lashes a Heavy Wound.

title: Retirement
heading: Retirement
summary: Older grogs may be retired after a serious aging crisis, and a retired grog still counts as a covenant member for finances.
quotes: the grog is still counted as a member of the covenant as far as its finances go

title: Pensions
heading: Pensions
summary: Describes the pensions covenants give retired grogs, how rent may substitute for a pension, and the treatment of widows.
quotes: Pensions are usually half to three-quarters of their former pay.

title: Horror stories for grogs
heading: Horror
summary: Advice for running horror, which leans on Personality Traits such as Brave and can represent madness as temporarily imposed high Personality Traits that govern reactions to certain stimuli.
quotes: Horror stories make extensive use of Personality Traits (particularly the Brave Trait)

title: Antagonists for grog stories
heading: Antagonists
summary: Guidance on choosing antagonists for grog-only stories, noting that grogs lack Magic Resistance so even weak supernatural powers threaten them, how a Brave roll can decide whether a band stands against a fear power, and how to keep a trained group from defeating the antagonist too early.
quotes: Grogs have no Magic Resistance at all

title: Rewards for grog stories
heading: Rewards
summary: Grogs earn experience like other characters but seldom gain vis or items, so the storyguide can reward success with experience in a Reputation among the covenfolk, favors, mentoring, an agency, or personalized equipment.
quotes: Grogs earn experience points at the same rate as any other character

title: All-Grog Sagas
heading: All-Grog Sagas
summary: Introduces sagas in which players run only grogs while magi are storyguide characters, and suggests running a grog saga in parallel with a standard saga, possibly with an alternative storyguide.
quotes: One saga deals with the actions of the magi, the other the consequences that those actions have on the turb

title: A Noble Saga
heading: A Noble Saga
summary: Describes a saga built on a noble household where the lord and a few select staff are companions and everyone else, including his sons of age, are grogs because they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.
quotes: Even the baron's sons who have reached their majority could be considered grog characters, since they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.

title: A Redcap Saga
heading: A Redcap Saga
summary: Explains that the Redcap Virtue is normally unavailable to grogs because it is a Major Social Status Virtue, and offers two fixes: make it a free Virtue for all characters or have the player characters work for redcaps instead.
quotes: allow the Redcap Virtue as a free Virtue
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages ch.3

title: Putting Together Your Team
heading: Putting Together Your Team
summary: A grog expedition needs a full complement of five roles, and the size of a trained group is capped by the leader's Leadership, with a limit on how far apart the members' Combat Totals can be.
quotes: An individual can only lead a band of grogs as a trained group equal in size to his score in the Leadership Ability.
no more than a 5 point difference between any of the Combat Totals

title: Commanding Larger Groups
heading: Commanding Larger Groups
summary: A leader can command a group larger than his Leadership score through subordinates who command their own men, at the cost of higher Ease Factors for whole-group Leadership rolls and commands that take his whole action.
quotes: have Ease Factors 3 higher than normal
A leader can usually only have a number of men under his command equal to his Leadership score.

title: Dux, the Leader
heading: Dux, the Leader
summary: The dux coordinates the band in combat, runs the expedition day to day, and is the liaison for orders from the magi; a good Leadership score is essential.
quotes: an essential feature is a good score in the Leadership Ability

title: Optio, the Second in Command
heading: Optio, the Second in Command
summary: The optio ensures the leader's orders are carried out and takes over if the leader falls, so should have the second-best Leadership and complementary skills.
quotes: The optio should have the second-best Leadership score in the unit.

title: Antesignanus, the Vanguard
heading: Antesignanus, the Vanguard
summary: The vanguard stands at the front of any fight and is the most likely to be wounded, so toughness Virtues matter; combining the vanguard and leader roles risks the whole trained group dissolving if he falls.
quotes: it dissolves into an untrained group immediately

title: Immune, the Specialist
heading: Immune, the Specialist
summary: The immune is the team's specialist, chosen to suit the expedition (commonly a chirurgeon); one without basic combat skills cannot be part of the trained group.
quotes: If an immune does not have basic combat skills, he cannot be a member of the trained group.

title: Signifer, the Legate
heading: Signifer, the Legate
summary: The signifer looks after the troop's internal tensions, pay and morale, speaks for the magi to mundanes, and is chosen for social skills such as Folk Ken and Carouse.
quotes: the signifer takes care of the internal tensions of the troop

title: The Grog Pack
heading: The Grog Pack
summary: Lists the equipment each grog carries on expeditions according to the liber gregis and states the Load of a pack, noting that it can be dropped without using an action so need not count in combat.
quotes: each grog pack imposes a Load of 4

title: Encumbrance and Ability Use
heading: Encumbrance and Ability Use
summary: Encumbrance penalizes physical activities and Fatigue rolls, but for climbing, swimming and balancing the storyguide uses Burden instead as the penalty to Ability rolls.
quotes: use Burden rather than Encumbrance as a penalty to Ability rolls

title: Equipment Bonuses (optional rule)
heading: Equipment Bonuses
summary: Optional rule letting non-essential equipment reduce the Ease Factor of an Ability roll by a minor or major amount, with only one bonus per roll and matching penalties for poor equipment.
quotes: Minor assistance subtracts 1 from the Ease Factor, whereas major assistance subtracts 3.

title: Encumbrance and Load
heading: Encumbrance and Load
summary: Converts Load to weight, gives the maximum weight a character can carry, lift, push or drag by Burden relative to Strength, the help from pulleys and levers, and how four-footed beasts calculate Encumbrance.
quotes: 1 Point of Load = 7 pounds
Burden equal to (Strength + 5)
Burden equal to (Strength + 12)

title: Equipment Bonuses table
heading: Equipment Bonuses
summary: Example table of pieces of equipment, the Ability and specialty they assist, and whether the help is minor or major.

title: Expanded Encumbrance Table
heading: Expanded Encumbrance Table
summary: Table converting Total Load to weight in pounds and to Burden for heavy loads.

title: Sentries (watch on expedition)
heading: Sentries
summary: On expedition each watch is shared by one or two men who stand one watch then rest for the next three, with no day and night patrol distinction.
quotes: There are eight watches in a day, each lasting three hours.

title: Weight of Common Materials
heading: Weight of Common Materials
summary: Table of weights per cubic foot of common materials with how many cubic feet fit in a Target: Individual, plus a table converting Size to a weight range.
quotes: A +1 increase in Size doubles the weight

title: Guides and Messengers
heading: Guides and Messengers
summary: Grogs plan journeys by itinerary and local knowledge, use Area Lore for navigation, and a successful Area Lore roll when planning a long journey can cut the travel time.
quotes: The Area Lore Ability is used for all sorts of navigation rolls
Intelligence + Area Lore roll of Ease Factor 12

title: Travel Speeds
heading: Travel Speeds
summary: How far characters travel in a day on foot, horseback, by cart, coach or ship, including forced marches that cost Long-Term Fatigue, the effect of Athletics and Ride, changing horses, and how encumbrance and cross-country travel reduce distance.
quotes: 15 + (2 x Athletics) on good roads
30 + (2 x Ride) on good roads

title: Travel Fatigue
heading: Travel Fatigue
summary: Table of typical miles per day by mode of transport, with and without taking Long-Term Fatigue.

title: Representatives
heading: Representatives
summary: Grogs often speak for magi because of The Gift; this section covers how bribes work, rough wages for context, and how a bribe of a day's or a week's pay gives a Minor or Major equipment bonus.
quotes: A bribe equivalent to a day's pay grants a Minor equipment bonus (see earlier), whereas a bribe equivalent to a week's pay grants a Major equipment bonus.

title: Gaining Information
heading: Gaining Information
summary: Getting locals to talk uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll, with the Ease Factor raised by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.
quotes: An average Communication + Folk Ken roll is usually sufficient to get an individual to talk, but increase the Ease Factor by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.

title: Negotiation (Bargain)
heading: Negotiation
summary: Procedure for haggling over a price: appraise the goods' value, make opposed Bargain rolls for buyer and seller, derive the lowest final price from the difference, and optionally roll to read the seller's willingness.
quotes: The buyer can attempt to determine the value by making a Perception + Bargain roll, with an Ease Factor of 9.
Communication + Bargain + simple die for the buyer and seller
Regardless of how good the buyer's Bargain roll is, the sale price is never less than half of the initial value.

title: Purchasing Supplies for Travel
heading: Purchasing Supplies for Travel
summary: Where and when grogs can buy food while traveling, with example prices and a rule of thumb for what it costs to feed a grog for a day.
quotes: Broadly speaking, it costs a Mythic Penny to feed a grog for a day, if you are buying rather than growing his food.

title: Arranging Accommodation
heading: Arranging Accommodation
summary: Finding lodging in remote places uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll against an Ease Factor set by the kind of accommodation, with The Gift's social penalty applying if the peasants have talked with the magi.
quotes: make a Communication + Folk Ken roll, using the Ease Factors in the following table

title: Translation
heading: Translation
summary: Rules for communicating across languages: rolls needed at low Language scores, how fluency limits use of social Abilities, and penalties to both speakers for dialect differences and related languages.
quotes: A character with a Language Ability of 2 or less needs to make Communication + Language rolls to get his point across
Unless she is fluent (Language Ability 5 or better), use of a character's social Abilities is limited by her Language score.

title: Personality Traits for grogs
heading: Personality Traits
summary: Suggests troupes make greater use of Personality Trait rolls for grogs, gives the usual starting Traits (Brave and Loyal), and says a Personality Flaw can be matched with an extra Trait at a set value.
quotes: Most grogs should have a Brave and a Loyal Personality Trait.
This trait should have a value of +3 (for a Minor Flaw) or +6 (for a Major Flaw).
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40

title: Making Personality Trait Rolls
heading: Making Personality Trait Rolls
summary: How to decide a character's action with a Personality Trait roll, how to treat opposed Traits and Personality Flaws, and how conflicting Traits shift the Ease Factor.
quotes: add the Personality Trait to the result of a stress die

title: Growing Used to The Gifted
heading: Growing Used to The Gifted
summary: People can grow used to a Gifted individual over time, so grogs use the covenant's Prevailing Loyalty rather than the magus's Gift penalty for Loyal rolls, with an optional system of separate Loyalty scores per magus.
quotes: An individual grog begins with a Loyal Personality Trait that is up to 3 points different from the turb's Prevailing Loyalty.

title: Advanced Group Combat
heading: Advanced Group Combat
summary: Introduces optional rules that add tactical depth to the core Group Combat rules, first printed in Lords of Men, which troupes may use or skip as drama and preference dictate.
quotes: The rules in this section expand the Group Combat rules in **ArM5** to add a bit more tactical depth.

title: The Leader's Actions
heading: The Leader's Actions
summary: A group leader gets one command roll per round without spending his action, and a member who stays in the group but does something other than attack is not counted for the group's combat bonus or damage.
quotes: A group leader can make one command-related die roll per round without using his action for that round.

title: Morale and Discipline
heading: Morale and Discipline
summary: Optional rules that weaken groups somewhat but make the leader important even for untrained groups, by requiring discipline and morale checks in battle.
quotes: Effective group tactics require both discipline and morale.

title: Discipline
heading: Discipline
summary: A Discipline roll, which takes no action, is needed when a group is tempted to break formation; failure leaves the group Disordered. The roll uses the leader's Presence and Leadership, with example Ease Factors by event.
quotes: stress die + Leader's Presence + Leader's Leadership
If a Discipline roll fails, the group temporarily becomes Disordered.

title: Morale
heading: Morale
summary: Groups make Morale rolls, which take no action, when bad things happen on the battlefield; failure makes the group Disordered and a failure while already Disordered routs it. The group may gain a bonus from its members' Brave scores, and example Ease Factors are listed.
quotes: stress die + Leader's Pre + Leader's Leadership
A group that fails a morale check becomes Disordered.

title: Disordered Groups
heading: Disordered Groups
summary: Effects of a Disordered group: a trained group functions as an untrained one, an untrained Disordered group can only land part of its attacks, and a further failed Morale check routs it.
quotes: A trained group that is Disordered functions as an untrained group.

title: Routed Groups
heading: Routed Groups
summary: A routed group has lost its will to fight and tries to Disengage and flee, possibly scattering; a group is routed if already Disordered and it fails a Morale check.
quotes: A group can become Routed if it is already Disordered and then fails a Morale check.

title: Rallying a Group
heading: Rallying a Group
summary: The leader spends an action on a Presence + Leadership roll to improve a Routed group to Disordered or a Disordered group to normal, with Ease Factors set by the group's situation and raised by casualties.
quotes: Presence + Leadership + stress Die

title: Groups With No Leader
heading: Groups With No Leader
summary: Optional rules for groups that lose their vanguard or leader: a group without a vanguard cannot attack but uses its best member's Defense, replacing a vanguard or taking over command is done by a Presence + Leadership roll, and a leaderless group automatically fails Morale and Discipline checks.
quotes: Leader's Presence + Leadership vs. Ease Factor 9
Presence + Leadership vs. Ease Factor 9
A group with no leader automatically fails any future Morale or Discipline checks.

title: Battlefield Injuries (activity while wounded)
heading: Battlefield Injuries
summary: Describes how Wound Penalties restrict travel, strenuous activity, sentry duty and double watches, and why a first-aider's Chirurgy matters for the Wound Recovery roll that prevents a wound from worsening.
quotes: Even a –1 Wound Penalty prohibits strenuous activity without risking the wound.

title: First Aid
heading: First Aid
summary: A chirurgeon can make a First Aid roll against the Improvement Ease Factor of a patient's worst wound to treat him as one category higher for Activity While Injured for a day; a botch provokes an immediate Wound Recovery roll.
quotes: Dexterity + Chirurgy + Recovery Modifiers (see Art & Academe, page 54) + Magical Aid + stress die vs Improvement Ease Factor

title: Magical First Aid
heading: Magical First Aid
summary: Hermetic spells and enchantments that prevent wounds from worsening or help recovery, including Bind Wound, low-level Creo Corpus bonuses to Wound Recovery, Endurance of the Berserkers, and a Sun-duration Chirurgeon's Healing Touch that causes Warping.
quotes: prevents any wound from worsening while in effect

title: The Death of a Grog
heading: The Death of a Grog
summary: How grogs treat their dead: washing the body, the role of Extreme Unction (which can be performed by any baptized person but protects the spirit for a limited time only when performed by an ordained priest), burial in consecrated ground, and the loss of Prevailing Loyalty if magi insist a body be abandoned.
quotes: can result in the loss of Prevailing Loyalty
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.75

title: Virtues and Flaws (changing them over time)
heading: Virtues and Flaws
summary: Characters can change their Virtues and Flaws over time; established characters may swap a Minor for a Minor or a Major for a Major with troupe approval, without touching Characteristics or Abilities or a feature of earlier stories.
quotes: a Minor Flaw can be exchanged for another Minor Flaw, and a Major Flaw for a Major Flaw, and the same applies to Virtues

title: Gaining New Flaws
heading: Gaining New Flaws
summary: Characters can gain Flaws through misfortune or action, but changed circumstances only become a Flaw when they affect the game, and grogs should not gain Story Flaws unless temporary or heading for transformation.
quotes: The storyguide should be careful not to allow a grog character to gain a Story Flaw

title: Changes in Social Status
heading: Changes in Social Status
summary: When a character's standing changes, such as promotion to custos or taking Holy Orders, the old Social Status Virtue or Flaw is simply replaced by the new one except where its description says both are kept.
quotes: simply replace the old Social Status Virtue with the new one

title: Gaining Flaws Through Mishaps
heading: Gaining Flaws Through Mishaps
summary: General Flaws, especially physical ones, are most often gained through misfortune such as amputations, battlefield injuries and diseases.
quotes: Most often, General Flaws are gained through mishap, particularly those that affect the body.

title: Gaining Flaws Through Actions
heading: Gaining Flaws Through Actions
summary: Actions can change social status or, with the storyguide's approval, bring Story Flaws such as a feud or debt, though grogs are usually barred from Story Flaws during play as in creation; offending a faerie can bring a Malediction or disfigurement.
quotes: although grogs are usually prohibited from gaining Story Flaws during the game

title: Gaining Flaws Through Magic
heading: Gaining Flaws Through Magic
summary: Curses from hedge wizard traditions are usually limited in duration, supernatural creatures can impose permanent Flaws at a cost to their Might, and Warping gives Flaws to characters not aligned to a Realm.
quotes: Warping induces the acquisition of Flaws in those characters who are not aligned to a Supernatural Realm
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.109

title: Gaining New Virtues
heading: Gaining New Virtues
summary: New Virtues are gained through magic, initiation or actions; a newly gained Virtue that affects experience does not retroactively change experience already gained.
quotes: this does not affect any experience points gained thus far

title: Gaining Virtues Through Magic
heading: Gaining Virtues Through Magic
summary: Supernatural sources can grant Virtues temporarily or permanently, such as gruagach spells, Objects of Virtue, faerie wizardry, Goetic Arts and creatures who give up Might; severe Warping can also confer Virtues.
quotes: The acquisition of Virtues in this manner should never be frivolous
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.114

title: Gaining Virtues Through Initiation
heading: Gaining Virtues Through Initiation
summary: Initiation into a mystery cult or hedge tradition grants Virtues after the character builds a score in the relevant Organization Lore and pays through ordeals, quests, sacrifice and study; grogs most commonly are initiated into the Ceremony Ability.
quotes: The character must develop a score in the Organization Lore of the cult or tradition in question before even being considered for Initiation.

title: Gaining Virtues Through Actions
heading: Gaining Virtues Through Actions
summary: Actions in stories, usually social interaction with storyguide characters, can give the effects of a Virtue such as Social Contacts or Protection, but a grog should be cautious about gaining a Major Virtue.
quotes: The troupe should be cautious about a grog gaining a Major Virtue

title: Losing Flaws
heading: Losing Flaws
summary: Most methods of gaining Virtues can also remove Flaws, though not every method suits every Flaw, and stories can lift curses.
quotes: Most of the methods by which Virtues can be gained (see earlier) can also rid a character of Flaws

title: Character Transformation (grog to companion)
heading: Character Transformation
summary: Explains how a grog can be turned into a companion when a story justifies it, with the troupe ensuring the new Virtues and Flaws suit the transformation and not padding Flaws just for more Virtue points.
quotes: The chief game difference between grogs and companions is the number and type of Virtues and Flaws

title: Inauguration
heading: Inauguration
summary: A transformation route in which a character is invested with temporal or spiritual authority and changes social status, such as becoming dean of a guild or a landed noble.
quotes: Those events which result in the investiture of a character with temporal or spiritual authority are termed inaugurations.

title: Metamorphosis
heading: Metamorphosis
summary: A transformation route in which a magical change permanently turns a character into something else, often granting Supernatural Virtues and Flaws of the relevant realm.
quotes: Metamorphosis often results in the acquisition of Supernatural Virtues and Flaws from the appropriate realm.

title: Initiation (as transformation)
heading: Initiation
summary: Initiation into a mystery cult can transform a grog into a companion, and is the route most likely to produce a Mythic Companion, a magus-equivalent character.
quotes: initiation is perhaps the most likely to produce a Mythic Companion, which is a magus-equivalent character

title: Pilgrimage (as transformation)
heading: Pilgrimage
summary: Any story or arc that takes a character out of his routine, tests him and changes his life can serve as a pilgrimage and justify transforming a grog into a companion.
quotes: Any story or story arc that takes a character out of his normal routine and location, tests his character, and then transforms his life forever is a pilgrimage.

title: Starting Characteristics
heading: Starting Characteristics
summary: Table of ready-made arrays of eight Characteristic scores bought with the standard number of points, from which a player can simply pick one for a grog.

title: Characteristics (grog creation)
heading: Characteristics
summary: Grogs buy Characteristics with the standard point pool, optionally taking negative points for more, or choose a pre-made array from the Starting Characteristics table.
quotes: Every character has 7 points to spend on buying positive Characteristics

title: Aging, the Easy Way
heading: Aging, the Easy Way
summary: A shortcut for aging old or many characters by looking up the Aging Points gained per decade for mild, average or harsh aging at the character's Aging Score, with a simple-die method to find Apparent Age.
quotes: age/10 (round up) – Living Conditions modifier – Longevity Ritual modifier

title: Aging Chart
heading: Aging Chart
summary: Table of expected Aging Points and crises per decade by Aging Score for mild, average and harsh aging, excluding points from crises.
quotes: The Aging Points listed exclude those deriving from crises.

title: Applying Crises
heading: Applying Crises
summary: Optional use of the crises listed on the Aging Chart: the character gains a Decrepitude score equal to the crises and additional Aging Points that shrink by fraction with each extra crisis, rounded up.
quotes: if he suffers one crisis, then he gets half of the Aging Points listed in the Aging Chart

title: Effects of Aging on Characteristics
heading: Effects of Aging on Characteristics
summary: Gives the approximate distribution of Aging Points among Characteristics so they can be applied in line with the Aging Table.
quotes: The Aging Table (**ArM5**, page 170) is designed to affect certain Characteristics in favor of others.

title: Childhood Training Packages
heading: Childhood Training Packages
summary: Lists the core childhood packages in training-package format plus two new ones, Covenant-bred and Feral, each granting experience in Abilities for the first years of life.
quotes: These packages can only be taken for the first five years of life.

title: Covenant-Bred Childhood
heading: Covenant-Bred Childhood
summary: A childhood package for characters raised in a covenant, giving experience in Area Lore: Covenant, Latin and Organization Lore: Order of Hermes among others.
quotes: This childhood is only available to characters with the Covenant Upbringing Personality Flaw.

title: Feral Childhood
heading: Feral Childhood
summary: A childhood package for characters raised wild, giving experience in survival and animal-related Abilities.
quotes: This childhood is only available to characters with the Feral Upbringing Flaw.
